selected_mechanism.name: Koniag/Tuknik ANC Corporate Stack: ANCSA Sovereign Capital Loop to Army Agentic AI

news_trigger.headline: KGS Subsidiary and Army Customer Win 2026 ACT-IAC Innovation Impact Award
news_trigger.verbatim_span: Koniag Government Services (KGS) supports the Office of the Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Army (Procurement) (ODASA(P)) in development of its Army Contracting Agentic AI Suite through its Tuknik Government Services (TGS) subsidiary... These intelligent automation solutions save over $37 million and 687,000 work hours annually by automating procurement processes.

selected_mechanism.one_line_definition: A five-layer ANCSA sovereign capital loop by which Koniag, Inc. (ANCSA regional corporation) channels federal AI-procurement revenue downward through holding company Koniag Government Services and 8(a)-protégé Tuknik Government Services — using a GSA STARS III task order — then repatriates profits upward to approximately 3,400 Alutiiq shareholders as dividends, converting a federal AI contract into Alaska Native sovereign wealth through a statutory preference unavailable to non-ANC firms.

layers.what_it_does: Koniag, Inc., one of 12 ANCSA regional corporations established by Congress in 1971, holds the sovereign charter that confers on its subsidiaries the ANC preference in federal contracting — specifically, entity-owned 8(a) participants (ANCs) are eligible for sole-source contracts above standard dollar thresholds, a privilege non-ANC small businesses do not have. This statutory foundation is what makes every downstream layer possible.
layers.controlling_actor: Koniag, Inc. Board of Directors (elected by ~3,400 Alutiiq shareholders); institutional role persists regardless of board composition

layers.layer_name: L2: Operating Holding Company (Koniag Government Services LLC)
layers.what_it_does: KGS aggregates contract vehicles and capabilities across Koniag's government services portfolio. It holds GSA OASIS+ (contracts 47QRCA26DA023, 47QRCA25DS893, 47QRCA25DU551), GSA MAS (IT Professional Services 54151S), SeaPort NxG (N0017825D7522), and GSA Polaris (47QTCC25DS061), plus AWS AI Specialization. KGS routes task orders to the appropriate subsidiary — in this case, Tuknik — and holds the commercial AI infrastructure relationships that underpin the Army suite.
layers.controlling_actor: KGS executive leadership; VP AI Strategy Carin Chapman as named capability owner; institutional role as holding company persists

layers.layer_name: L3: 8(a) Delivery Subsidiary and GWAC Vehicle (Tuknik Government Services, STARS III #47QTCB22D0301)
layers.what_it_does: Tuknik Government Services is the 8(a)-certified delivery entity holding GSA STARS III master contract 47QTCB22D0301 — a $50B government-wide acquisition contract for IT services. STARS III's base ordering period runs July 2, 2021 through July 1, 2026; GSA has announced intent to exercise a 3-year option extending the ordering period through July 1, 2029. TGS receives task orders under STARS III and executes the Army Contracting Agentic AI Suite. The ANC 8(a) preference that eliminates competitive bidding requirements flows through TGS's 8(a) certification.
layers.controlling_actor: GSA Federal Acquisition Service Contracting Officer for STARS III (institutional role) — holds binary authority to execute or not execute the option period modification before July 1, 2026; TGS Program Manager Sam Coulson on the delivery side

layers.layer_name: L4: Federal Customer Task Order (ODASA(P) Army Procurement Agentic AI Suite)
layers.what_it_does: The Office of the Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Army (Procurement) issues task orders against TGS's STARS III vehicle for development and operation of the Army Contracting Agentic AI Suite: over 150 automated workflows including DORA (Determination of Responsibility Assistant), J&A Jump Starter, PAMela Chatbot, and AI-Powered User Public Square — all running on Amazon Bedrock. The suite saves $37M and 687,000 work hours annually. ODASA(P) sets scope and funding for each task order; new task orders after July 1, 2026 depend on the STARS III option being exercised.
layers.controlling_actor: ODASA(P) (Office of the Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Army for Procurement) as task-order issuing authority; KGS/TGS as prime contractor; AWS as cloud infrastructure provider

layers.layer_name: L5: ANC Profit Repatriation and Shareholder Benefit Layer
layers.what_it_does: Federal task-order revenue flows from ODASA(P) to TGS to KGS to Koniag, Inc., where it is distributed to approximately 3,400 Alutiiq shareholders as dividends, educational scholarships, elder distributions, and community investments. This is the sovereignty closure: federal AI-procurement spending becomes Alaska Native sovereign wealth, routed through a statutory preference that converts federal contract dollars into indigenous economic capital unavailable through any other contracting pathway.
layers.controlling_actor: Koniag, Inc. Board of Directors (elected by Alutiiq shareholders); institutional role as ANCSA regional corporation distribution authority persists regardless of board composition

chokepoint.layer_name: L3: STARS III Option Period Execution
chokepoint.actor: GSA Federal Acquisition Service Contracting Officer for STARS III (institutional role)
chokepoint.binary_decision: Execute or decline to execute the contract modification extending the STARS III ordering period from July 1, 2026 through July 1, 2029 — a single bilateral modification that either keeps the task-order pipeline open for three additional years or closes new-order authority on July 1, 2026
chokepoint.why_asymmetric: The GSA Contracting Officer for STARS III is the single institutional role with unilateral authority to execute the option period modification. No other party — not Koniag, not ODASA(P), not TGS — can substitute for that signature. GSA has announced intent to exercise but has not yet executed the formal modification. Until the modification is signed, every new task order placed after July 1, 2026 under STARS III — including any Army AI suite expansion — is at risk.

selected_mechanism.structural_read: The Koniag/Tuknik corporate stack is a template for how ANCSA regional corporations have evolved from land-settlement vehicles into federal AI prime contractors. The loop is elegant: ANCSA sovereign status → 8(a) certification → GWAC vehicle access → sole-source task-order eligibility → federal AI revenue → shareholder dividend repatriation. The July 1, 2026 STARS III chokepoint reveals a structural fragility in this loop — every ANC firm using STARS III faces the same option-period cliff simultaneously. GSA's published intent to exercise does not eliminate execution risk; it signals intent, not completion. Any ANC operating company with STARS III exposure should be treating the option modification signature as a binary event requiring active vendor relationship management with GSA's Federal Acquisition Service.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: Any Alaska-based ANC operating company (or their legal/contracts team) with active STARS III task orders should confirm with GSA's Federal Acquisition Service whether the STARS III option period modification has been formally executed — not merely announced as intent — and if not, request a written status update and any transition or bridge-contract mechanism in the event of a gap. The July 1 cliff is 31 days out.
selected_mechanism.ak_consequence: Koniag's ~3,400 Alutiiq shareholders receive dividends from $250M+ in federal AI revenues routed through the ANCSA corporate stack; the GSA STARS III option-period modification — which must be executed before July 1, 2026 — is the single binary event determining whether TGS can continue writing new Army AI task orders through 2029 or faces a 31-day ordering gap that disrupts the repatriation loop.
